claims.text: The initial alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a single-phase BCC microstructure.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance under high-temperature service conditions.
Pack-cementation aluminizing of as-cast HfNbTaTiZr will form a thin, continuous, adherent alumina scale.
The aluminized layer will have a graded interface with the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
Treatment at approximately 1100 °C for 2 hours in argon is suitable for producing the proposed protective coating.
Controlling aluminized depth and coating thickness will improve coating performance.
An alumina barrier has sufficiently low oxygen permeability to retard oxygen diffusion into the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
A graded coating–substrate interface will reduce thermal-expansion stresses.
Reducing interfacial thermal stresses will prevent or reduce oxide-scale spallation during thermal cycling.
The alumina barrier and graded interface will preserve the bulk mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr.
Aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will have markedly better oxidation resistance than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr in air at approximately 1000 °C.
The oxidation-resistance benefit will persist for exposures of 50–100 hours.
After aluminizing and high-temperature exposure, the alloy will retain 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
After aluminizing and high-temperature exposure, the alloy will retain a high-temperature yield strength of 163–530 MPa.
The proposed performance boundary applies near 1000 °C in oxidizing atmospheres at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1 for up to 100 hours.
